messages.text: Please also answer, as far as possible - the comments on the PR
I’ll review each thread against the latest changes, post answers with links to the evidence, and identify the questions that still need research.

I’ve replied to the geometry and redesign threads, and explained why MAG-06’s viability remains open. The physics agent’s main conclusion is that independent muon momentum measurement does not inherently require a separately powered magnet: an instrumented return field could provide it, if sufficient bending occurs between independent measurements. I’ll post the requested pro/con issue and link it from the two physics threads.

All seven review threads now have replies. [Issue #9](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/issues/9) contains the physics agent’s pro/con assessment and proposed tests. I’ve left the threads open for the reviewer and made clear that standalone performance and MAG-06 feasibility remain unproven.

Replied to **all seven comments** on [PR #6](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/6), linking the revised designs and validation evidence.

Created [issue #9](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/issues/9) with the physics agent’s return-field versus dedicated-magnet pro/con assessment.

Standalone performance and MAG-06 feasibility remain explicitly open. Threads await reviewer confirmation.

Responses and assessment are recorded in Git; documentation, dashboard and logging checks passed.
